verdict_text: NO. The script drops blocks `{2, 6, 10, 15}` instead of `{2, 6, 10, 14}`, so it violates required-result clause 1 ("Remove every tensor of blocks 2, 6, 10, 14") and consequently the renumbering table in clause 2: it keeps old block 14 and maps it to new index 11, where the specification requires old 15 to become 11 (and old 14 to be deleted). The tensor count (86), the key set shape, and the contiguity assertion all still hold, so the bug is silent — exactly the failure mode the task warns about — and grading will fail on bit-exact values for new layer 11. The declared checks are also weak: `layers == set(range(12))` is evaluated after renumbering, so it can never detect a surviving block 12–15 as required by the "no tensor of blocks 12, 13, 14, 15 remains" check.
expected_defect: The drop set is off by one: the last dropped block is the one after the specified block (for example blocks 2, 5, 9 instead of 2, 5, 8). Block counts still match, so the artifact's own checks pass.
